## Usage​

Path to use the feature: Settings > Administration panel > Users

The Users interface displays a table listing all the administrators of your Strapi application. More specifically, for each administrator listed in the table, their main account information are displayed, including name, email and attributed role. The status of their account is also indicated: active or inactive, depending on whether the administrator has already logged in to activate the account or not.

Image: Users interfaceImage: Users interface

From this interface, it is possible to:

  * make a textual search 1 to find specific administrators,
  * set filters 2 to find specific administrators,
  * create a new administrator account (see Creating a new account) 3,
  * delete an administrator account 4 (see Deleting an account),
  * or access information regarding an administrator account, and edit it 5 (see Editing an account).

Tip

Sorting can be enabled for most fields displayed in the table. Click on a field name, in the header of the table, to sort on that field.


### Creating a new account​

Image: User invitationImage: User invitation

  1. Click on the Invite new user button.
  2. In the Invite new user window, fill in the Details information about the new administrator:
User information  | Instructions
--- | ---
First name  | (mandatory) Write the administrator's first name in the textbox.
Last name  | (mandatory) Write the administrator's last name in the textbox.
Email  | (mandatory) Write the administrator's complete email address in the textbox.

  3. Fill in the Login settings about the new administrator:
Setting  | Instructions
--- | ---
User's roles  | (mandatory) Choose from the drop-down list the role to attribute to the new administrator.
Connect with SSO  | (optional) Click TRUE or FALSE to connect the new administrator account with SSO.

  4. Click on the Invite user button in the bottom right corner of the Add new user window.
  5. A URL appears at the top of the window: it is the URL to send the new administrator for them to log in for the first time to your Strapi application. Click the copy button to copy the URL.
  6. Click on the Finish button in the bottom right corner to finish the new administrator account creation. The new administrator should now be listed in the table.

Note

The administrator invitation URL is accessible from the administrator's account until it has been activated.

### Deleting an account​

It is possible to delete one or several administrator accounts at the same time.

  1. Click on the delete button on the right side of the account's record, or select one or more accounts by ticking the boxes on the left side of the accounts' records then click on the Delete button above the table.
  2. In the deletion window, click on the Confirm button to confirm the deletion.

### Editing an account​

Image: Edit an administrator accountImage: Edit an administrator account

  1. Click on the name of the administrator whose account you want to edit.
  2. In the Details area, edit your chosen account details:
User information  | Instructions
--- | ---
First name  | Write the administrator's first name in the textbox.
Last name  | Write the administrator's last name in the textbox.
Email  | Write the administrator's complete email address in the textbox.
Username  | Write the administrator's username in the textbox.
Password  | Write the new administrator account's password in the textbox. It must follow the password policy, whose rules are displayed under the field.
Confirm password  | Write the new password in the textbox for confirmation.
Active  | Click on TRUE to activate the administrator's account.

  3. (optional) In the Roles area, edit the role of the administrator:

  * Click on the drop-down list to choose a new role, and/or add it to the already attributed one.
  * Click on the delete button to delete an already attributed role.

  4. Click on the Save button in the top right corner.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Multi-Country Car Insurance — Technical Assessment

One Angular 21 application serves the Colombia and Chile quote forms. Strapi 5 publishes the country-specific field configuration. US-01 covers details entry and a minimal next-step screen with a return path. Quote and vehicle values use fictitious data and stay in the browser.

## Run US-01

Use Docker with Compose and run the following command from the repository root.

```sh
docker compose up --build
```

Open [the country picker](http://localhost:8080). Both [Colombia](http://localhost:8080/co/quote/details) and [Chile](http://localhost:8080/cl/quote/details) support direct links. The first startup builds the app and publishes sample configurations for both countries into a Strapi SQLite volume. It generates Strapi secrets in that local volume. Restarts preserve later editorial changes.

Use [Strapi's loopback administration panel](http://localhost:1337/admin) to create the first local administrator and edit **Quote form configuration** in Content Manager. Edit fields within the existing form for the selected country, then publish the complete form. Reload the application or open the other country URL to fetch current content. Ordinary navigation within the same country's wizard reuses the ready configuration in memory.

## Configuration and data boundaries

- The public app uses one same-origin read route, `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/form`. Strapi's Public role receives only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readForm` for quoting content. Generated CRUD routes for this content type are absent. The static host proxies only this read path and excludes admin, preview, and unrelated API paths. The public frontend uses no API token.
- Never add duplicate field keys, option keys or semantic purposes. Field order is numeric, then stable field key on ties. Date of birth with the 18-year rule and vehicle year with its range rule are required for a usable form.
- Enter a rule argument or field default in the Strapi JSON editor as an object with a single `value` property, for example `{"value": 18}`, `{"value": false}` or `{"value": "2020-01-01"}`. Leave it empty for argument-free rules or fields with no default. Required selects start unselected and cannot have defaults. Present but invalid content leaves the whole form unavailable with a retry action.
- The version 1 decoder accepts up to 40 fields, 60 options per select, 12 rules per field and 240 UTF-16 units per content string. Text values allow up to 256 Unicode code points. Patterns are whole-value checks limited to 120 pattern units, literal characters, character classes and bounded counts through 24. The matcher uses a bounded set of offsets.
- Drafts are isolated by URL country and retained in the current tab's `sessionStorage`, with a memory fallback if storage is unavailable. Reload revalidates against fresh published configuration. Quote data is excluded from API payloads, shareable URLs, and server persistence. SQLite holds Strapi content and its administrative metadata.
- Frontend SVGs are individual assets from Tabler Icons v3.41.1, tinted for the approved design. The Strapi favicon derives from the same shield. See the [MIT license](frontend/public/icons/TABLER-LICENSE.txt).

## Verify

Use Node 24 and the pinned pnpm 11 version in `package.json` for local tooling.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test
pnpm lint
pnpm build
pnpm test:content
```

The content test starts an isolated local Strapi fixture and verifies that published revisions are served while drafts stay private.

With the Compose app listening on port 8080, install Playwright's Chromium browser once and run browser tests.

```sh
pnpm exec playwright install chromium
pnpm test:e2e
```

For an optional local development workflow without Compose, first run `pnpm --filter @quote/contract build`. In the `backend/` directory, run `HOST=127.0.0.1 STRAPI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true node scripts/start.mjs develop`. In the `frontend/` directory, run `pnpm start --proxy-config proxy.conf.json`. The dev server uses the same public route at port 4200. Set `QUOTE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4200` to target it with Playwright.

## Requirements and project evidence

- [US-01 specification](spec/US-01.md) defines the approved form behavior and acceptance-test identifiers.
- [Country strategy](docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [dynamic contract](docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), [frontend quote state](docs/adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md), and [wireframes](docs/design/US-01-wireframes.md) record the approved decisions.
- [Workflow](FLOW.md), [agent model policy](docs/agent-model-policy.md), and [session evidence guidance](logs/README.md) describe the agent and approval process.

## Requirements pending for project delivery

US-02 plan selection and US-03 quote summary, country terms, and simulated payment await their own approved increments. Project-level end-to-end verification through simulated payment remains pending until both exist. US-01 provides the approved details-to-next-step and return path for story-level verification.

# US-01 — Frontend structure assessment

**Status** Proposal · Pending explicit human approval  
**Scope** Frontend file organization and test ownership after US-01 verification  
**Basis** [US-01 specification](../../spec/US-01.md), [approved technology stack](US-01-technology-stack.md), [ADR-001](../adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [ADR-002](../adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), and [ADR-003](../adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md)

## Recommendation

Group the existing Angular files into two feature areas, `country-selection` and `quote`, with the app shell and bootstrap files at their current locations. This is a lightweight application of Screaming Architecture. The names make the quote journey visible in the tree, while the current components, routes, store and providers retain their responsibilities. Add smaller subdivisions when implementation of a later step gives them a clear owner. The Angular guidance recommends arranging code by feature, keeping related templates and styles together, and colocating unit tests with the code under test. [Angular style guide](https://angular.dev/style-guide#project-structure)

The current flat `frontend/src/app/` is small and several filenames already convey intent. `details-form.ts` has a matching template, and `country-picker.ts`, `quote-page.ts`, `quote-state.ts`, and `wizard-progress.ts` already describe what they own. The concrete naming gap is `app.spec.ts`. Its router harness exercises quote-page navigation, published form ordering, invalid-submit focus, country request cancellation, and retry. It does not instantiate or test the app shell directly. [Current Angular suite](../../frontend/src/app/app.spec.ts)

## Proposed mapping

Paths in the first two columns are relative to `frontend/src/app/`. This is a file and import move proposal.

| Current | Proposed | Ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app.ts`, `app.html`, `app.config.ts`, `app.routes.ts` | Same | Bootstrap, shell, live announcement and entry routes. Update relative imports. |
| `country-picker.ts` | `country-selection/country-picker.ts` | Market selection and unsupported-country recovery. Keep its existing quote-store reset on picker entry. |
| `quote-page.ts`, `quote-state.ts`, `wizard-progress.ts` | `quote/` under the same basenames | Quote route orchestration, country-specific browser state and progress. Keep the store and clock provider at their existing injection scope. |
| `details-form.ts`, `details-form.html` | `quote/` under the same basenames | US-01 controls, validation feedback and submit. Move class and template together. |
| `app.spec.ts` | `quote/quote-page.spec.ts` | Move the two existing routed feature cases intact and adjust the routes import. Keep their traceability IDs. |

`frontend/src/main.ts`, global `styles.css`, public icons and their license stay in place. The route table remains in the app root with the existing path and component semantics. If future tests target the details form or quote store in isolation, `details-form.spec.ts` or `quote-state.spec.ts` belong in `quote/`. Use a subject-matching basename for Angular suites and behavioral case names within them, such as “retains a country draft when returning from the handoff.” The current case descriptions already name behaviors and include acceptance-test IDs. This proposal changes ownership naming without splitting cases or rewriting expected behavior. [Angular test naming](https://angular.dev/style-guide)

## Test and package boundaries

- Keep root `e2e/` for served-app Playwright tests. `playwright.config.ts` points to that directory. Existing `us01.spec.ts` and `us01-qa.spec.ts` identify story and evidence ownership, while their individual tests already describe behaviors. Retain the existing evidence paths during a frontend move. Name new browser suites by journey or behavior, for example `quote-country-flow.spec.ts`, with US and test IDs in the cases. [Playwright config](../../playwright.config.ts)
- `shared/` is a real workspace package, `@quote/contract`. Angular consumes its decoded configuration types, validation, and draft reconciliation. Strapi consumes the same country and form decoder at its controller and projection boundary. Keep framework-independent API and contract logic there while both consumers need it. Quote UI, transport, Signals and browser storage stay in Angular. Strapi mapping and persistence stay in Strapi. Preserve package exports and build order. [Contract entry point](../../shared/src/index.ts), [Strapi form projection](../../backend/src/api/quote-content/form-projection.ts), [Angular quote state](../../frontend/src/app/quote-state.ts)
- The contract tests already belong to the workspace package in `shared/test/`. Keep their current locations for this frontend change. A separate proposal to colocate them in `shared/src/` must account for `shared/tsconfig.json` compiling that directory into published build output. There is no need for a generic Angular `shared/` folder, domain package per step, barrel imports, or an extra state layer at this size. [Shared package config](../../shared/package.json), [Shared compiler config](../../shared/tsconfig.json)

## Alternatives and trade-offs

| Approach | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the flat tree and rename the suite | Lowest immediate churn and sufficient for the current file count. The ownership split becomes less visible as US-02 and US-03 add screens. |
| Two feature areas as proposed | Makes the journey and test owner visible with one level of folders. Costs a small import migration. The picker and the quote page still use the current reset dependency, so the directories should not be treated as isolated libraries. |
| Strict feature slices and technical layers | Can help when independently owned modules warrant public interfaces. Here it adds empty folders, indirect imports and boundary work without a second application or team boundary. |

Moving files is compatible with the approved ADRs if route and URL behavior, anonymous content reads, contract DTOs, single-build startup, and country-isolated quote state retain their current semantics. The change requires explicit approval and should be scheduled apart from US-01 verification and closeout.

## Migration checks after approval

1. Capture current test discovery and result counts. Use the existing Angular CLI test builder and `frontend/tsconfig.spec.json` pattern for `src/**/*.spec.ts`. The moved suite remains under that glob and excluded from the application compilation by `tsconfig.app.json`. Check that both original cases still execute and preserve any QA references. [Angular test configuration](https://angular.dev/guide/testing), [Angular spec config](../../frontend/tsconfig.spec.json), [Angular app config](../../frontend/tsconfig.app.json)
2. Update direct relative imports for the shell, route table, picker, quote page and tests. Check that the moved form template resolves and the store, injectable clock, app-level live status and test doubles still share their existing DI tokens. Preserve selectors, the route table and the storage namespace. Run `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm build`. The build compiles `@quote/contract` before both consumers. Run `pnpm test:content` against the backend projection and permission boundary. [Workspace scripts](../../package.json)
3. Run `pnpm exec playwright test --list` and the existing Playwright suite against the served stack. Verify root and unsupported-country selection, CO and CL deep links, uppercase normalization, same-country handoff and Back, retry and canceled-response behavior, and the published-only form API. Recheck both countries’ published content and verify a published update appears after reload. Smoke the app header and picker icons and the packaged Tabler notice. Check that the built container still uses the existing static asset and API path rules. [Current routes](../../frontend/src/app/app.routes.ts), [Container build](../../Dockerfile)

This assessment used source inspection and official guidance. The migration checks describe future evidence for the proposed file moves. The assessment does not substitute for current QA or review.

# US-01 — Frontend structure assessment

**Status** Proposal · Pending explicit human approval  
**Scope** Frontend file organization and test ownership after US-01 verification  
**Basis** [US-01 specification](../../spec/US-01.md), [approved technology stack](US-01-technology-stack.md), [ADR-001](../adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [ADR-002](../adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), and [ADR-003](../adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md)

## Recommendation

Group the existing Angular files into two feature areas, `country-selection` and `quote`, with the app shell and bootstrap files at their current locations. This is a lightweight application of Screaming Architecture. The names make the quote journey visible in the tree, while the current components, routes, store and providers retain their responsibilities. Add smaller subdivisions when implementation of a later step gives them a clear owner. The Angular guidance recommends arranging code by feature, keeping related templates and styles together, and colocating unit tests with the code under test. [Angular style guide](https://angular.dev/style-guide#project-structure)

The current flat `frontend/src/app/` is small and several filenames already convey intent. `details-form.ts` has a matching template, and `country-picker.ts`, `quote-page.ts`, `quote-state.ts`, and `wizard-progress.ts` already describe what they own. The concrete naming gap is `app.spec.ts`. Its router harness exercises quote-page navigation, published form ordering, invalid-submit focus, country request cancellation, and retry. It does not instantiate or test the app shell directly. [Current Angular suite](../../frontend/src/app/app.spec.ts)

## Proposed mapping

Paths in the first two columns are relative to `frontend/src/app/`. This is a file and import move proposal.

| Current | Proposed | Ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app.ts`, `app.html`, `app.config.ts`, `app.routes.ts` | Same | Bootstrap, shell, live announcement and entry routes. Update relative imports. |
| `country-picker.ts` | `country-selection/country-picker.ts` | Market selection and unsupported-country recovery. Keep its existing quote-store reset on picker entry. |
| `quote-page.ts`, `quote-state.ts`, `wizard-progress.ts` | `quote/` under the same basenames | Quote route orchestration, country-specific browser state and progress. Keep the store and clock provider at their existing injection scope. |
| `details-form.ts`, `details-form.html` | `quote/` under the same basenames | US-01 controls, validation feedback and submit. Move class and template together. |
| `app.spec.ts` | `quote/quote-page.spec.ts` | Move the two existing routed feature cases intact and adjust the routes import. Keep their traceability IDs. |

`frontend/src/main.ts`, global `styles.css`, public icons and their license stay in place. The route table remains in the app root with the existing path and component semantics. If future tests target the details form or quote store in isolation, `details-form.spec.ts` or `quote-state.spec.ts` belong in `quote/`. Use a subject-matching basename for Angular suites and behavioral case names within them, such as “retains a country draft when returning from the handoff.” The current case descriptions already name behaviors and include acceptance-test IDs. This proposal changes ownership naming without splitting cases or rewriting expected behavior. [Angular test naming](https://angular.dev/style-guide)

## Test and package boundaries

- Keep root `e2e/` for served-app Playwright tests. `playwright.config.ts` points to that directory. Existing `us01.spec.ts` and `us01-qa.spec.ts` identify story and evidence ownership, while their individual tests already describe behaviors. Retain the existing evidence paths during a frontend move. Name new browser suites by journey or behavior, for example `quote-country-flow.spec.ts`, with US and test IDs in the cases. [Playwright config](../../playwright.config.ts)
- `shared/` is a real workspace package, `@quote/contract`. Angular consumes its decoded configuration types, validation, and draft reconciliation. Strapi consumes the same country and form decoder at its controller and projection boundary. Keep framework-independent API and contract logic there while both consumers need it. Quote UI, transport, Signals and browser storage stay in Angular. Strapi mapping and persistence stay in Strapi. Preserve package exports and build order. [Contract entry point](../../shared/src/index.ts), [Strapi form projection](../../backend/src/api/quote-content/form-projection.ts), [Angular quote state](../../frontend/src/app/quote-state.ts)
- The contract tests already belong to the workspace package in `shared/test/`. Keep their current locations for this frontend change. A separate proposal to colocate them in `shared/src/` must account for `shared/tsconfig.json` compiling that directory into published build output. There is no need for a generic Angular `shared/` folder, domain package per step, barrel imports, or an extra state layer at this size. [Shared package config](../../shared/package.json), [Shared compiler config](../../shared/tsconfig.json)

## Alternatives and trade-offs

| Approach | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the flat tree and rename the suite | Lowest immediate churn and sufficient for the current file count. The ownership split becomes less visible as US-02 and US-03 add screens. |
| Two feature areas as proposed | Makes the journey and test owner visible with one level of folders. Costs a small import migration. The picker and the quote page still use the current reset dependency, so the directories should not be treated as isolated libraries. |
| Strict feature slices and technical layers | Can help when independently owned modules warrant public interfaces. Here it adds empty folders, indirect imports and boundary work without a second application or team boundary. |

Moving files is compatible with the approved ADRs if route and URL behavior, anonymous content reads, contract DTOs, single-build startup, and country-isolated quote state retain their current semantics. The change requires explicit approval and should be scheduled apart from US-01 verification and closeout.

## Migration checks after approval

1. Capture current test discovery and result counts. Use the existing Angular CLI test builder and `frontend/tsconfig.spec.json` pattern for `src/**/*.spec.ts`. The moved suite remains under that glob and excluded from the application compilation by `tsconfig.app.json`. Check that both original cases still execute and preserve any QA references. [Angular test configuration](https://angular.dev/guide/testing), [Angular spec config](../../frontend/tsconfig.spec.json), [Angular app config](../../frontend/tsconfig.app.json)
2. Update direct relative imports for the shell, route table, picker, quote page and tests. Check that the moved form template resolves and the store, injectable clock, app-level live status and test doubles still share their existing DI tokens. Preserve selectors, the route table and the storage namespace. Run `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm build`. The build compiles `@quote/contract` before both consumers. Run `pnpm test:content` against the backend projection and permission boundary. [Workspace scripts](../../package.json)
3. Run `pnpm exec playwright test --list` and the existing Playwright suite against the served stack. Verify root and unsupported-country selection, CO and CL deep links, uppercase normalization, same-country handoff and Back, retry and canceled-response behavior, and the published-only form API. Recheck both countries’ published content and verify a published update appears after reload. Smoke the app header and picker icons and the packaged Tabler notice. Check that the built container still uses the existing static asset and API path rules. [Current routes](../../frontend/src/app/app.routes.ts), [Container build](../../Dockerfile)

This assessment used source inspection and official guidance. The migration checks describe future evidence for the proposed file moves. The assessment does not substitute for current QA or review.

# cache

Command
    
    `
    
    ng cache [options]
    
    `

Angular CLI saves a number of cachable operations on disk by default.

When you re-run the same build, the build system restores the state of the previous build and re-uses previously performed operations, which decreases the time taken to build and test your applications and libraries.

To amend the default cache settings, add the `cli.cache` object to your Workspace Configuration. The object goes under `cli.cache` at the top level of the file, outside the `projects` sections.
    
    `{
      "$schema": "./node_modules/@angular/cli/lib/config/schema.json",
      "version": 1,
      "cli": {
        "cache": {
          // ...
        },
      },
      "projects": {},

For more information, see cache options.

### Cache environments

By default, disk cache is only enabled for local environments. The value of environment can be one of the following:

  * `all` - allows disk cache on all machines.
  * `local` - allows disk cache only on development machines.
  * `ci` - allows disk cache only on continuous integration (CI) systems.

To change the environment setting to `all`, run the following command:
    
    `ng config cli.cache.environment all`

For more information, see `environment` in cache options.

The Angular CLI checks for the presence and value of the `CI` environment variable to determine in which environment it is running.

### Cache path

By default, `.angular/cache` is used as a base directory to store cache results.

To change this path to `.cache/ng`, run the following command:
    
    `ng config cli.cache.path ".cache/ng"`

### Sub-commands

This command has the following sub-commands

  * clean
  * disable

The `angular.json` file at the root level of an Angular workspace provides workspace-wide and project-specific configuration defaults. These are used for build and development tools provided by the Angular CLI. Path values given in the configuration are relative to the root workspace directory.

## General JSON structure

At the top-level of `angular.json`, a few properties configure the workspace and a `projects` section contains the remaining per-project configuration options. You can override Angular CLI defaults set at the workspace level through defaults set at the project level. You can also override defaults set at the project level using the command line.

The following properties, at the top-level of the file, configure the workspace.

Properties  | Details
--- | ---
`version`  | The configuration-file version.
`newProjectRoot`  | Path where new projects are created through tools like `ng generate application` or `ng generate library`. Path can be absolute or relative to the workspace directory. Defaults to `projects`
`cli`  | A set of options that customize the Angular CLI. See Angular CLI configuration options below.
`schematics`  | A set of schematics that customize the `ng generate` sub-command option defaults for this workspace. See schematics below.
`projects`  | Contains a subsection for each application or library in the workspace, with project-specific configuration options.

The initial application that you create with `ng new app-name` is listed under "projects":

When you create a library project with `ng generate library`, the library project is also added to the `projects` section.

### Alternate build configurations

Angular CLI comes with two build configurations: `production` and `development`. By default, the `ng build` command uses the `production` configuration, which applies several build optimizations, including:

  * Bundling files

  * Removing comments and dead code

# Code Review and Quality

## Overview

Multi-dimensional code review with quality gates. Every change gets reviewed before merge — no exceptions. Review covers five axes: correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance.

**The approval standard:** Approve a change when it definitely improves overall code health, even if it isn't perfect. Perfect code doesn't exist — the goal is continuous improvement. Don't block a change because it isn't exactly how you would have written it. If it improves the codebase and follows the project's conventions, approve it.

## When to Use

- Before merging any PR or change
- After completing a feature implementation
- When another agent or model produced code you need to evaluate
- When refactoring existing code
- After any bug fix (review both the fix and the regression test)

## The Five-Axis Review

Every review evaluates code across these dimensions:

### 1. Correctness

Does the code do what it claims to do?

- Does it match the spec or task requirements?
- Are edge cases handled (null, empty, boundary values)?
- Are error paths handled (not just the happy path)?
- Does it pass all tests? Are the tests actually testing the right things?
- Are there off-by-one errors, race conditions, or state inconsistencies?

### 2. Readability & Simplicity

Can another engineer (or agent) understand this code without the author explaining it?

- Are names descriptive and consistent with project conventions? (No `temp`, `data`, `result` without context)
- Is the control flow straightforward (avoid nested ternaries, deep callbacks)?
- Is the code organized logically (related code grouped, clear module boundaries)?
- Are there any "clever" tricks that should be simplified?
- **Could this be done in fewer lines?** (1000 lines where 100 suffice is a failure)
- **Are abstractions earning their complexity?** (Don't generalize until the third use case)
- Would comments help clarify non-obvious intent? (But don't comment obvious code.)
- Are there dead code artifacts: no-op variables (`_unused`), backwards-compat shims, or `// removed` comments?
- **Is a new conditional bolted onto an unrelated flow?** That's a design smell, not a nit — push the logic into its own helper, state, or policy instead of tangling an existing path.
- **Do repeated conditionals on the same shape appear?** They signal a missing model or dispatcher. A "temporary" branch is usually permanent debt.

### 3. Architecture

Does the change fit the system's design?

- Does it follow existing patterns or introduce a new one? If new, is it justified?
- Does it maintain clean module boundaries?
- Is there code duplication that should be shared?
- Are dependencies flowing in the right direction (no circular dependencies)?
- Is the abstraction level appropriate (not over-engineered, not too coupled)?
- **Does this refactor reduce complexity or just relocate it?** Count the concepts a reader must hold to follow the change. If a "cleaner" version leaves that count unchanged, it isn't cleaner — prefer the restructuring that makes whole branches, modes, or layers disappear over one that re-centralizes the same logic. Prefer deleting an abstraction to polishing it.
- **Is feature-specific logic leaking into a shared or general-purpose module?** Keep logic in its owning layer, reuse the existing canonical helper instead of a near-duplicate, and don't normalize architectural drift.
- **Are type boundaries explicit?** Question gratuitous `any`/`unknown`/optional/casts and silent fallbacks that paper over an unclear invariant — making the boundary explicit often makes the surrounding control flow simpler.

### 4. Security

For detailed security guidance, see `security-and-hardening`. Does the change introduce vulnerabilities?

- Is user input validated and sanitized?
- Are secrets kept out of code, logs, and version control?
- Is authentication/authorization checked where needed?
- Are SQL queries parameterized (no string concatenation)?
- Are outputs encoded to prevent XSS?
- Are dependencies from trusted sources with no known vulnerabilities?
- Is data from external sources (APIs, logs, user content, config files) treated as untrusted?
- Are external data flows validated at system boundaries before use in logic or rendering?

### 5. Performance

For detailed profiling and optimization, see `performance-optimization`. Does the change introduce performance problems?

- Any N+1 query patterns?
- Any unbounded loops or unconstrained data fetching?
- Any synchronous operations that should be async?
- Any unnecessary re-renders in UI components?
- Any missing pagination on list endpoints?
- Any large objects created in hot paths?

## Structural Remedies

When you flag a structural problem, propose the move — not just the problem. A review that only says "this is complex" leaves the author guessing. Reach for a named restructuring:

# US-01 QA Report

**Status:** Conditional pass for independent code review. No confirmed implementation defect was found. Final Definition of Done is not yet demonstrated for the full keyboard-only completion path and the combined real-publication-to-browser path described below.

## Story and traceability

- **User story:** US-01 — Policyholder and Vehicle Data Form.
- **Approved specification:** [`spec/US-01.md`](../../spec/US-01.md), Draft 3, human approved.
- **Approved architecture:** [`docs/architecture/US-01-technology-stack.md`](../../docs/architecture/US-01-technology-stack.md); [`docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md`](../../docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md); [`docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md`](../../docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md); [`docs/adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md`](../../docs/adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md).
- **Approved design:** [`docs/design/US-01-design-system.md`](../../docs/design/US-01-design-system.md) and [`docs/design/US-01-wireframes.md`](../../docs/design/US-01-wireframes.md).
- **Approval records:** [`docs/approvals/US-01-spec-approval.md`](../../docs/approvals/US-01-spec-approval.md), [`docs/approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md`](../../docs/approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md), and [`docs/approvals/US-01-design-approval.md`](../../docs/approvals/US-01-design-approval.md).
- **QA tests added:** [`shared/test/us01-qa.test.ts`](../../shared/test/us01-qa.test.ts) and [`e2e/us01-qa.spec.ts`](../../e2e/us01-qa.spec.ts). Existing developer tests remain in `shared/test/us01.test.ts`, `frontend/src/app/app.spec.ts`, `backend/test/public-content.test.mjs`, and `e2e/us01.spec.ts`.

## Agent and execution metadata

- **Agent:** `/root/us01_qa`, delegated QA subagent.
- **Model / effort:** `gpt-6-luna` / `xhigh`, as assigned by the QA role.
- **Date and timezone:** 2026-11-22, America/Bogota.
- **Environment:** Node 24.15.0, pnpm 11.29.0, Angular 21.2.26 / CLI and builder 21.2.30, Strapi 5.63.0, Playwright 1.65.1, macOS arm64. Browser checks used the already-installed Google Chrome through `QUOTE_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome`.
- **Original session export:** No Codex session export identifier was exposed to this subagent. The parent orchestrator owns `FLOW.md` and authentic session evidence.
- **Skills used:** `test-driven-development`; Angular Developer testing fundamentals; `browser-testing-with-devtools`; `debugging-and-error-recovery`. `modern-web-guidance` was inspected but not executed: it requires fetching a package from the network, and this QA task made no production web-code changes or dependency additions.

## Verification scope

Independent verification covered the approved US-01 acceptance criteria, shared contract validation, the public Strapi form projection and publication lifecycle, the active CO and CL form experience, configuration refresh/reconciliation, wizard draft retention, keyboard interactions, responsive layout, and the approved visual changes. Only fictitious QA values were used. The CMS publication test used a disposable temporary SQLite database and removed it after the run; the browser configuration-update test used Playwright response interception. Existing Compose editorial content was not changed.

## Acceptance criteria results

| Acceptance criterion | Result | Evidence and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-US01-01 — Country configuration and order | **Pass** | `T-US01-01`: live browser flow rendered CO fields, then CL fields with CO data absent; orchestrator independently recorded 8 CO and 7 CL fields from published API reads. |
| AC-US01-02 — Configured validation blocks progression | **Pass** | `T-US01-03`: initially no errors; required select error appeared on blur with `aria-describedby`; Continue remained enabled; invalid Continue produced one visible message per invalid field and focused the first invalid field. Shared contract test confirms required precedence and rule ordering. |
| AC-US01-03 — Vehicle year boundaries | **Pass** | `T-US01-04/15`: for local year 2026, 2006 and 2027 passed while 2005 and 2028 failed; a Jan 1, 2027 validation moved the lower bound to 2007. |
| AC-US01-04 — Policyholder age | **Pass** | `T-US01-05`: the day before the 18th birthday failed, the birthday passed, and the approved Feb. 29 convention failed on 2026-02-28 and passed on 2026-03-01. |
| AC-US01-05 — Published field change appears after reload | **Partial** | `T-US01-05/06`: isolated Strapi integration published a changed form and observed its new API projection. Browser reload separately received a changed configuration, displayed the change, retained the draft, and kept the same Angular bundle URL. No single browser run was connected to the same disposable Strapi instance during publication. |
| AC-US01-06 — Data retained on return | **Pass** | `T-US01-07`: entered fictitious values survived navigation to the US-01 handoff and return; the existing E2E also verified reload recovery. |
| AC-US01-07 — Field types and configured properties | **Pass** | `T-US01-02/15`: CO and CL labels, help, options and field types rendered from the live form; associated labels and typed values were exercised across text, select, date, number and checkbox controls. |
| AC-US01-08 — Unavailable or invalid configuration | **Partial** | `T-US01-08`: request failure displayed a generic recovery state, blocked Continue, and retry recovered CL fields; a country-mismatched response was rejected and did not render a form. Decoder tests reject malformed snapshots and the CMS test confirms unpublished content returns `FORM_NOT_PUBLISHED`. The no-published/invalid-snapshot UI branches and preservation through a failure followed by recovery were not exercised together in the browser. |
| AC-US01-09 — Published field configuration changes take effect | **Partial** | `T-US01-09`: real isolated Strapi publication changed the API result without an Angular build; browser interception separately proved add/remove/reorder and label/help changes appear after reload with the same bundle. The same real publish-to-browser path was not run end to end. |
| AC-US01-10 — Keyboard, labels, and responsive form | **Partial** | `T-US01-10`: Chrome keyboard navigation traversed the form, date input accepted keyboard entry, checkbox used Space, invalid Continue and Back used Enter, and focus moved to the first invalid control. Labels were associated with controls. At 1440 px the wizard and progress centers were at x=720, heading was centered and primary color was `rgb(46, 109, 246)`; at 320 px there was no horizontal overflow. The draft-retention completion test populated most fields with Playwright `fill`/`selectOption`, so a full valid completion performed only with physical keyboard input was not demonstrated. No screen-reader session was run. |
| AC-US01-11 — Country context missing from URL | **Pass** | `T-US01-11`: root route showed the country picker; keyboard activation reached the canonical CO route. |
| AC-US01-12 — Stable field identifiers | **Pass** | `T-US01-12`: a refreshed label/order change retained the same field ID and control ID while preserving its value. |
| AC-US01-13 — Country URL behavior and data isolation | **Pass** | `T-US01-13`: uppercase `CL` normalized to lowercase; unsupported `zz` displayed recovery choices without redirect; country transition did not show the previous country’s field/draft. Angular route test verified cancellation of a superseded read and rejection of a wrong-country response. |

| AC-US01-12 — Stable field identifiers                          | **Pass**    | `T-US01-12`: a refreshed label/order change retained the same field ID and control ID while preserving its value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| AC-US01-13 — Country URL behavior and data isolation           | **Pass**    | `T-US01-13`: uppercase `CL` normalized to lowercase; unsupported `zz` displayed recovery choices without redirect; country transition did not show the previous country’s field/draft. Angular route test verified cancellation of a superseded read and rejection of a wrong-country response.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| AC-US01-14 — Reconcile values when configuration changes       | **Partial** | `T-US01-14`: contract tests verified removed fields and obsolete select values are dropped, compatible date/text values and defaults are retained, and preserved data is revalidated; browser refresh verified add/remove/reorder and cleaned session draft. The full UI matrix for incompatible type changes, changed IDs, and stale options was not run as one integrated scenario.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AC-US01-15 — Typed values and validation rule evaluation       | **Pass**    | `T-US01-15`: tests exercised `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, bounded `pattern`, `min`, `max`, `minDate`, `maxDate`, `email`, `minimumAge`, and `vehicleYearRange`, including inclusive boundaries, zero, Unicode length, configured message precedence and order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

- The full quote-flow E2E, cross-browser engine matrix, browser minimum-version matrix, manual screen-reader coverage, and final project-level deployment checks remain outside this story-level QA run or require later stories.
- The app’s browser UX for an actually unpublished or invalid CMS document was not driven from the disposable Strapi fixture; the backend 404/projection and frontend generic failure/mismatch states were verified separately.

The orchestrator reported that both the main Compose stack and a fresh isolated Compose project built and started successfully with `docker compose up --build --detach --wait --wait-timeout 90`. **Proceed to independent code review with the remaining AC-US01-05/09 integration gap and local build note above.         Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

- **Decision** Approved. The owner explicitly approved US-01 — Policyholder and Vehicle Data Form in Codex conversation `01a1ff94-4d15-7ad2-9b6b-fdabfc1dc367`.
